text:
kai: Starting canary rollout of adaptive-gpu-metrics-agent v0.3 to us-west1-gpu-pool today 10:30 PT. Goal: reduce Prometheus ingestion ~40% with adaptive sampling + label normalization. Canary = 30 nodes.
jin: Quick Q — what does "adaptive sampling" actually change? Will we lose per-device or per-process detail?
maya: Also need to think billing; can't drop job attribution for Dedicated clusters.
kai: Short version: stable metrics get lower scrape frequency; bursty/critical metrics kept at full rate. When label cardinality for a metric exceeds threshold we synthesize a `device_group` label (e.g., many/unique) instead of keeping high-cardinality raw labels. We keep gpu_util and power_draw untouched.
samir: Sounds good. For hosted customers we should preserve job labels by default if pod label `redwood.billing=true` is present.
kai: Yep — config flag `preserve_job_labels: true` for dedicated/private; hosted fallback = only preserve when billing label present.
jin: Can you paste the Prometheus relabel/metric_relabel snippet you're testing?
kai: ```
relabel_configs:
  - source_labels: [__meta_kubernetes_pod_label_job_id]
    action: replace
    target_label: job_id
metric_relabel_configs:
  - source_labels: [device_label_count]
    regex: "^([6-9]|[1-9][0-9]+)$"
    action: replace
    target_label: device_group
    replacement: "many"
  - action: labeldrop
    regex: "^per_process_"
```
maya: Important: we need an opt-out for clusters doing fine with full cardinality. Add `preserve_labels: [job_id, user_id]` option.
samir: Alerts: plan to relax dcgm memory pressure alert threshold in canary for 2h and mute noisy per-process SLO alerts. Also add a short window to avoid flapping.
ops-bot: Deploy pipeline created: `deploy/adaptive-agent/canary/us-west1` — targets 30 nodes, 5% increment/min, health-check 1h between phases.
jin: I'll add a temporary Grafana panel to the infra board: /d/agent-canary to show sample counts, unique label counts, and agent error rate.
maya: I'll run a billing-attribution smoke test during the canary — ensure top-10 job owners still attributable.
samir: Cost estimate if successful: ~35% fewer ingested samples on GPU fleet -> ~22% monitoring spend drop across gpu clusters. We'll validate after 1h of steady state.
kai: Canary exit criteria: no missing critical metrics for 1h, agent error rate <0.1%, metric cardinality reduction >=25% in canary pool. If any fail, rollback to v0.2 automatically. Plan to ramp to full fleet after 8h of green.
jin: Minor note: make sure metrics with `exported_for_sla=true` are exempt.
maya: :thumbsup: LGTM from billing side. Ping me if top-N attribution diverges.
ops-bot: Canary started at 1876543210 (10:30 PT). Will post health updates here.
kai: Update after 45m: cardinality down 33%, agent error rate 0.03%, no new critical alerts. Proceeding to ramp to 60 nodes now.
ops-bot: Ramp event logged at 1876543525.
jin: Thanks team — I'll update the runbook with the relabel snippet and alert adjustments.
maya: Scheduling follow-up verification in 2h to compare billing metrics.
samir: If green after 8h, let's schedule global rollout overnight to minimize customer impact.
